CVE-2026-105154.title: Apache Roller: Cross-site request forgery in Planet administration lets an attacker make the server fetch arbitrary URLs
CVE-2026-105154.description: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) in the Planet feed aggregator administration of Apache Roller 4.0 through 6.1.6 allows an unauthenticated attacker to make the Roller server fetch a URL the attacker chooses, including internal addresses, by inducing a logged-in global administrator to open a crafted web page. The action that adds a Planet subscription can be triggered cross-site; in recent releases it accepts GET requests, which Roller's CSRF token check does not cover. The action fetches the supplied URL and saves the subscription, and any fetched content that parses as a feed is then published without authentication in the aggregated Planet feed. CVE-2026-115887.title: graphql-scalars PhoneNumber scalar is vulnerable to regular expression denial of service
CVE-2026-115887.description: GraphQL Scalars is a library of custom GraphQL scalars for creating precise type-safe GraphQL schemas. From 1.24.1 until 2.0.1, GraphQLPhoneNumber in src/scalars/PhoneNumber.ts uses ambiguous nested digit quantifiers that backtrack exponentially when a PhoneNumber value contains a run of digits followed by a character that makes the match fail. GraphQL evaluates parseLiteral during document validation and parseValue during variable coercion before resolver authentication or authorization, so a small unauthenticated request can block the Node.js event loop and stall the server process. serialize is also affected when unvalidated stored values are returned through the scalar. This issue is fixed in version 2.0.1.

CVE-2026-120308.title: Beta9 host filesystem exposure via volume path traversal
CVE-2026-120308.description: A Beta9 tenant can attach a volume when deploying a function, endpoint, or task queue. The gateway builds the host path by joining the shared volumes root, the workspace name, and the volume identifier from the stub configuration. Nothing checks that the identifier names a volume that workspace owns. Parent-directory segments in the identifier collapse the joined path to the worker's filesystem root, and the worker bind-mounts that path into the sandbox read-write unless the volume was explicitly marked read-only. A tenant with a workspace token can therefore read and write the worker's files, including other tenants' volumes stored on that machine. Confirmed against gateway 0.1.769 and worker 0.1.745. Fixed in gateway 0.1.776 and worker 0.1.756: volume identifiers and mount paths are validated before a mount is built, including for stubs saved before the check existed, and the gateway rejects a volume that does not exist or is not owned by the workspace.

CVE-2026-133429.title: Validation bypass of extra data keys in JSON model validation
CVE-2026-133429.description:
When validating JSON data into a model allowing extra data, the keys of extra data aren't validated against the key type annotated on __pydantic_extra__, resulting in extra data not matching the declared type. This is the case if you define __pydantic_extra__ as e.g. dict[Annotated[str, Field(pattern=r'^x_')], int].

The validate_json_by_iteration() method (in pydantic-core/src/validators/model_fields.rs), used to validate JSON data into models, only validates the values of extra data, and stores the keys as is.

The issue was fixed in commit 4c65dbda9970a488e2ff21c8693fc6f6d70a3358.

Impact: validation bypass, as extra data returned by validation doesn't match the declared type. Affected are applications validating untrusted JSON data into models allowing extra data (with extra='allow'), with a key type annotated on __pydantic_extra__ (e.g. dict[Annotated[str, Field(pattern=...)], int]), using Pydantic from 2.13.0 up to (but excluding) 2.14.2.

Python mode validation isn't affected.

CVE-2026-98874.title: wifi: iwlwifi: mld: don't WARN on WoWLAN suspend w/o netdetect
CVE-2026-98874.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

wifi: iwlwifi: mld: don't WARN on WoWLAN suspend w/o netdetect

Clearly, from a user perspective, it must be valid to configure
WoWLAN and then suspend while not connected to a network. Since
mac80211 doesn't distinguish these cases and simply calls the
driver to suspend whenever WoWLAN is configured, the driver has
to cleanly handle the case where it's called for WoWLAN, it's
not connected but there's also no netdetect configured.

Remove the WARN_ON() and keep returning 1 to disconnect and
then suspend.

CVE-2026-99334.title: KVM: PPC: Book3S HV: Add preempt_disable() around virtual-mode HPTE bit-lock users
CVE-2026-99334.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: PPC: Book3S HV: Add preempt_disable() around virtual-mode HPTE bit-lock users

kvmppc_hv_find_lock_hpte() requires virtual-mode callers to run with
preemption disabled, because it can return with HPTE_V_HVLOCK still held
until the caller later unlocks the HPTE. Existing virtual-mode callers
in book3s_64_mmu_hv.c already follow that rule.

Two virtual-mode call paths do not:

1. kvmppc_handle_exit_hv() calls kvmppc_hpte_hv_fault() for hash-mode
data-side and instruction-side faults after guest exit, with
preemption already enabled. kvmppc_hpte_hv_fault() calls
kvmppc_hv_find_lock_hpte() directly.

2. kvmppc_pseries_do_hcall() executes virtual-mode handlers for HPT
hcalls via kvmppc_pseries_do_hpt_hcall() with preemption enabled.
The handlers for H_ENTER, H_REMOVE, H_READ, H_CLEAR_MOD, H_CLEAR_REF,
H_PROTECT, and H_BULK_REMOVE spin on try_lock_hpte() or lock_rmap(),
and H_ENTER also reaches kvmppc_do_h_enter(),…

CVE-2026-99381.title: smb: client: reject short or out-of-range FIND response parameters
CVE-2026-99381.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: reject short or out-of-range FIND response parameters

CIFSFindFirst() and CIFSFindNext() read the SearchHandle, SearchCount,
EndofSearch and LastNameOffset of a TRANS2_FIND_FIRST2 or
TRANS2_FIND_NEXT2 response at ParameterOffset. validate_t2() bounds
the offset at 1024 and ParameterCount below 512, and nothing compares
them with the number of bytes SendReceive() copied into the buffer or
with the size of the response parameters. smb_init() places the
request and the response in the same cifs_request allocation and
cifs_buf_get() clears only the start of it, so a short response with a
ParameterOffset past its end has the search handle, the entry count,
the end-of-search flag and the last-entry offset read out of the
request that was just sent, or out of whatever the allocation held
